cues.text: Answer and ask practical A2 questions about real family life, hobbies, food, restaurants, travel, summer plans, and this week.
Practice targets: Answer with one real detail: who, where, when, or why.
Use recently, usually, this summer, and next.
Choose practical topics first.
Ask one useful follow-up question.
Listen once to hear the questions and model starters.
In the lesson, start with the quick plan, then choose one card from each topic.
You do not need every question.
Quick Plan.
Start with the easiest topic so the conversation feels natural.
What do you want to talk about first today?
Starter: First, I want to talk about because.
Which topic is useful for your real life?
Which topic is easy to answer today?
Which topic do you want more English for?
Helpful expressions: This topic is easy for me.
I can use this in real life.
I want more words for this topic.
Today, I want to keep this topic light.
Quick Plan.
Choose a speaking style before the main questions.
How long do you want your answers to be today?
Starter: Today, I want to practise answers.
Do you want short and clear answers?
Do you want longer answers with reasons?
Do you want help with grammar or vocabulary?
Helpful expressions: I want to speak more smoothly.
I want to add one reason.
I need help with past tense.
I need useful phrases, not difficult words.
Kids and Family.
Talk about one recent change, interest, or small moment.
How have your children been recently?
Starter: They have been recently.
What have they been interested in recently?
Has anything changed with them?
What is one thing you want to remember from this time?
Helpful expressions: They have more energy than before.
They are interested in.
They talk about.
It is easier than before.
Kids and Family.
Use one normal routine from family life.
What is the busiest time at home these days?
Starter: The busiest time is because.
What usually happens at that time?
Who needs help first?
What makes that time easier?
Helpful expressions: They usually want a snack first.
I try to prepare before that time.
It is busy, but it is normal.
It helps when.
Hobbies and Golf.
Say yes or no, then add one real detail.
Have you had time for golf or another hobby recently?
Starter: Recently, I, and it was.
Where did you practise or enjoy it?
What did you work on?
What do you want to improve next?
Helpful expressions: I practised my swing.
I worked on.
It felt better than before.
I still need to improve.
Hobbies and Golf.
Talk about a realistic plan, not a perfect plan.
What hobby do you want more time for?
Starter: I want more time for, but.
Why do you want more time for it?
What stops you from doing it more?
When could you realistically do it?
Helpful expressions: It helps me relax.
It is hard to find time.
Maybe I could do it on.
A realistic plan is.
Food, Cooking, and Restaurants.
Use one food from real life at home.
What have you been cooking recently?
Starter: Recently, I have been cooking.
Is it easy to make?
Does your family like it?
What ingredient do you always need?
Helpful expressions: It is easy to make.
My family likes it.
I cook it when I am busy.
I usually need.
Food, Cooking, and Restaurants.
Talk about food at home, a cafe, or a restaurant.
Have you eaten anything good recently?
Starter: Recently, I ate, and it was.
Where did you eat it?
Who did you eat with?
Would you eat it again?
Helpful expressions: I ate it at.
I ate with.
I would eat it again.
The best part was.
Food, Cooking, and Restaurants.
Think about speed, space, menu, and noise.
What kind of restaurant or cafe is easiest with children?
Starter: restaurants are easy with children because.
What makes a restaurant difficult with children?
Is fast service important?
Is enough space important?
Helpful expressions: Fast service is important.
Enough space is important.
A simple menu helps.
It is difficult when.
Travel and Summer Plans.
Use this summer, might, or still thinking.
Do you have any plans for summer vacation?
Starter: This summer, we might.
Where are you thinking of going?
Is it easy with children?
What do you need to prepare?
Helpful expressions: We might go to.
We are still thinking.
We need to prepare.
It depends on.
Travel and Summer Plans.
Choose one real place, even if the plan is not decided.
What place in Japan are you interested in visiting?
Starter: I am interested in visiting because.
What would you like to do there?
Would it be a day trip or an overnight trip?
What season would be best?
Helpful expressions: I would like to.
It could be a day trip.
I think season is best.
It looks good because.
Weekly Life Catch-Up.
Finish with a simple review of the week and one next plan.
What was your week like overall?
Starter: My week was because.
Next, I want to.
What took most of your time?
What was one small success?
What are you looking forward to next?
Helpful expressions: It was a normal week.
Most of my time went to.
One small success was.
I am looking forward to.
What do you want to talk about first today?
How long do you want your answers to be today?
How have your children been recently?
What is the busiest time at home these days?
Have you had time for golf or another hobby recently?
What hobby do you want more time for?
What have you been cooking recently?
Have you eaten anything good recently?
What kind of restaurant or cafe is easiest with children?
Do you have any plans for summer vacation?
What place in Japan are you interested in visiting?
What was your week like overall?
A strong conversation answer has one real detail.
Say who, where, when, why, or what happened next.
Then the next question becomes natural.
